title: Choosing the Right AI Tool
description: A practical decision framework for picking the right AI tool for any task.

data.text: Having too many tool choices is its own problem. This lesson gives you a simple decision framework you can apply to any task in under 30 seconds. The goal is to stop second-guessing and start doing.

data.title: Ask these questions before choosing a tool

items.text: Does this task need verified, sourced facts?
Is this long document analysis or careful writing?
Am I working in Google Docs, Gmail, or Drive?
Do I need image generation or data analysis on a file?

items.hint: Check the tool's enterprise plan — most tools have a version with data privacy guarantees

items.text: Will the task be automated or run at scale?
items.hint: Prefer tools with robust APIs, rate limits, and enterprise controls

items.text: Do I need citations or an auditable trail?
items.hint: Prefer Perplexity or tools that return sources and logs

rows: Perplexity shows source for every claim
Edit or rewrite a long document
Gemini is native to Google Workspace
Both excellent, Copilot better for in-editor use
DALL-E 3 is built into ChatGPT Plus
Claude handles larger files more reliably
ChatGPT's code interpreter runs actual analysis
Get cited primary sources, not just AI opinion
Any works well — Gemini best for Gmail replies
Ask ChatGPT/Claude to explain; use Perplexity for supplementary facts

data.text: Using multiple tools for one task

Many workflows benefit from combining tools. Use Perplexity to research the facts, then Claude to write the article with those facts, then Gemini's Docs integration to insert it into your document. The tools are complementary, not mutually exclusive.

data.caption: Example multi-tool workflow: research → verify → synthesize → publish

data.text: The best tool changes month by month as models improve. Focus on learning the skill of prompt writing — that skill transfers across any tool that exists now or will exist in the future.

items: If you need sources: start with Perplexity.
If you need to paste a long document: start with Claude.
If you need to act inside Google Workspace: start with Gemini.
If you need images or code execution: start with ChatGPT (paid).
When in doubt, prototype in ChatGPT or Claude and add Perplexity for verification.

data.title: Decision shortcut
points: Long docs and careful writing → Claude
Images, data analysis, or general tasks → ChatGPT
Power users combine 2-3 tools in the same workflow
The skill of prompting matters more than the tool you choose

data.text: If you plan to connect production data, evaluate vendor enterprise features: data residency, training opt-out, audit logs, role-based access, and contractual SLAs. For regulated industries, prefer private instances or on-premise options where available.

rows: Where is data stored and processed?
Will vendor use my data to train models?
Opt out or use private instances
Can you restrict who can call write-capable tools?
Use least-privilege credentials and separate environments
Are tool calls and outputs logged immutably?
Enable logging and export to SIEM

data.text: Quick checklist before you pick a tool

items: Define the success criteria for the task (accuracy, format, citations).
Decide whether the output will be automated or human-reviewed.
Identify any sensitive data and choose enterprise controls if needed.
Prototype with a free tier to validate prompt patterns and edge cases.
Measure accuracy, cost, latency, and safety before scaling.

data.text: Run a short pilot with real inputs, measure the metrics above, and test failure modes (hallucinations, truncated context, permission misuse) before granting broad access.
